name: Squash and stretch
summary: A moving form changes shape but keeps its volume: it stretches along its path at speed and squashes on impact.
how: Keep the volume constant: when the height grows by a factor k, scale the width by 1/k.
Stretch along the path by 10% to 30% at the highest speed and squash by the same amount on impact.
In an interface, use a spring with a damping ratio of 0.6 to 0.8, so that an element overshoots once and settles.

origin.note: Disney animators exaggerate the volume of a ball and a face; Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston name it the first of twelve principles in 1981.

adoptions.via: John Lasseter applies it to computer animation in Luxo Jr. and in his SIGGRAPH paper of 1987.
Spring-damped animation in iOS 7 lets interface elements overshoot and settle.
3D motion design renders soft bodies that wobble, inflate and bounce.

sources.title: Frank Thomas and Ollie Johnston, The Illusion of Life: Disney Animation (1981)
John Lasseter, Principles of Traditional Animation Applied to 3D Computer Animation (SIGGRAPH, 1987)
